description: Proposed movement pattern hierarchy (OQ-22): family then pattern. relatedCategories on a family lists the existing exercise categories it usually accompanies; categories stay independent.

nodes.label: Lower-body compound
nodes.definition: Multi-joint movements that bend and straighten the hips and knees under load.
nodes.includes: Squat, hinge and lunge patterns.
nodes.excludes: Single-joint knee or hip work (Knee joint, Hip joint).

nodes.label: Squat
nodes.definition: Knees and hips bend together with the trunk fairly upright and both feet loaded.
nodes.includes: Barbell, goblet, hack and Smith squats; leg press; wall sit; sissy squat.
nodes.note: Leg press and wall sit are classed here: debatable.

nodes.label: Hinge
nodes.definition: The hips travel back and forward with a near-neutral spine; knees bend only a little.
nodes.includes: Deadlifts, Romanian deadlifts, good mornings, kettlebell swings, pull-throughs.
nodes.note: Kettlebell swing is a ballistic hinge.

nodes.label: Lunge and split stance
nodes.definition: One leg leads or carries most of the load while the other supports from behind or the side.
nodes.includes: Lunges, split squats, step-ups, single-leg squats, skater squats.
nodes.note: Single-leg hinges are Hinge with unilateral laterality.

nodes.label: Upper-body push
nodes.definition: Movements that press a load or the body away from the torso.
nodes.includes: Horizontal and vertical push.
nodes.excludes: Single-joint elbow extension and fly movements.

nodes.label: Horizontal push
nodes.definition: Pressing along a line roughly level with the chest, including inclines up to about 45 degrees.
nodes.includes: Bench and chest presses, push-ups, floor presses.
nodes.excludes: Overhead presses (Vertical push); flys (Shoulder horizontal adduction).
nodes.note: Incline angles above about 45 degrees count as vertical push.

nodes.label: Vertical push
nodes.definition: Pressing overhead or steeply upwards, or pushing the body upwards against the hands.
nodes.includes: Overhead presses, push presses, pike push-ups, dips.

nodes.label: Upper-body pull
nodes.definition: Movements that pull a load or the body towards the torso.
nodes.includes: Horizontal and vertical pull.
nodes.excludes: Single-joint elbow flexion and shoulder blade work.

nodes.label: Horizontal pull
nodes.definition: Pulling the hands towards the torso along a roughly horizontal line.
nodes.includes: Rows with any implement, inverted rows, seated cable rows.

nodes.label: Vertical pull
nodes.definition: Pulling the hands down towards the torso or the body up towards the hands.
nodes.includes: Pull-ups, chin-ups, lat pulldowns.

nodes.label: Elbow
nodes.definition: Single-joint movements at the elbow.
nodes.includes: Elbow flexion and extension.

nodes.label: Elbow flexion
nodes.definition: Bending the elbow against resistance.
nodes.includes: All curl variations.
nodes.excludes: Pull-ups and rows, which are compound pulls.

nodes.label: Elbow extension
nodes.definition: Straightening the elbow against resistance with the upper arm held in place.
nodes.includes: Pushdowns, skull crushers, overhead extensions, kickbacks.

nodes.label: Shoulder joint
nodes.definition: Single-joint movements of the arm at the shoulder.
nodes.includes: Abduction, flexion, extension, horizontal movements and rotation.

nodes.label: Shoulder abduction
nodes.definition: Raising the arm out to the side.
nodes.includes: Lateral raises, cable lateral raises, scaption.

nodes.label: Shoulder flexion
nodes.definition: Raising the arm forward and up.
nodes.includes: Front raises, plate raises.

nodes.label: Shoulder extension
nodes.definition: Pulling the straight arm down and back.
nodes.includes: Straight-arm pulldowns, dumbbell pullovers.
nodes.excludes: Rows and pulldowns with bent elbows.
nodes.note: Pullover is classed here: debatable (it also trains chest).

nodes.label: Shoulder horizontal adduction
nodes.definition: Bringing the arms together across the chest.
nodes.includes: Chest flys, cable crossovers, pec deck.

nodes.label: Shoulder horizontal abduction
nodes.definition: Moving the arms apart behind the line of the shoulders.
nodes.includes: Reverse flys, face pulls, band pull-aparts.

nodes.label: Shoulder external rotation
nodes.definition: Turning the upper arm outward.
nodes.includes: Cable and band external rotations, side-lying rotations.
nodes.excludes: Face pulls, which are horizontal abduction first.

nodes.label: Shoulder internal rotation
nodes.definition: Turning the upper arm inward.
nodes.includes: Cable and band internal rotations.

nodes.label: Shoulder blade
nodes.definition: Movements of the shoulder blade on the ribcage.
nodes.includes: Elevation, retraction, protraction, depression.
nodes.excludes: Arm movements at the shoulder joint.

nodes.label: Scapular elevation
nodes.definition: Lifting the shoulder blades towards the ears.
nodes.includes: Shrugs, upright-row shrug portion.

nodes.label: Scapular retraction
nodes.definition: Drawing the shoulder blades together.
nodes.includes: Scapular rows, prone Y-T-W, band retractions.

nodes.label: Scapular protraction
nodes.definition: Pushing the shoulder blades forward around the ribcage.
nodes.includes: Push-up plus, cable serratus punch.

nodes.label: Scapular depression
nodes.definition: Pulling the shoulder blades down away from the ears.
nodes.includes: Straight-arm scapular pulls, support holds on dip bars.

nodes.label: Knee
nodes.definition: Single-joint movements at the knee.
nodes.includes: Knee extension and flexion.

nodes.label: Knee extension
nodes.definition: Straightening the knee against resistance with the hip fixed.
nodes.includes: Leg extensions, band knee extensions, terminal knee extensions.

nodes.label: Knee flexion
nodes.definition: Bending the knee against resistance with the hip fixed.
nodes.includes: Leg curls, Nordic curls, slider curls, stability-ball curls.

nodes.label: Hip
nodes.definition: Single-joint movements at the hip.
nodes.includes: Extension, abduction, adduction, flexion, rotation.

nodes.label: Hip extension
nodes.definition: Driving the thigh back with the knee and trunk largely fixed.
nodes.includes: Hip thrusts, glute bridges, cable kickbacks, back extensions with hip drive.
nodes.note: Hip thrust is classed here rather than Hinge: debatable.

nodes.label: Hip abduction
nodes.definition: Moving the leg out to the side.
nodes.includes: Machine and cable abduction, side-lying raises, banded walks, clamshells.
nodes.excludes: Side planks (Anti-lateral flexion); squats with a band.

nodes.label: Hip adduction
nodes.definition: Moving the leg towards the midline.
nodes.includes: Machine and cable adduction, Copenhagen plank, squeeze-ball work.
nodes.excludes: Wide-stance compound lifts, which are classed by their main pattern.

nodes.label: Hip flexion
nodes.definition: Lifting the thigh towards the trunk.
nodes.includes: Hanging knee raises, hanging leg raises, standing cable knee drives, supine leg raises.
nodes.note: Hanging raises often pair hip flexion with trunk flexion.

nodes.label: Hip rotation
nodes.definition: Turning the thigh in or out at the hip.
nodes.includes: Seated and prone hip rotations, 90/90 transitions, banded external rotations.

nodes.label: Ankle and foot
nodes.definition: Single-joint movements at the ankle.
nodes.includes: Plantar flexion, dorsiflexion, inversion and eversion.

nodes.label: Plantar flexion
nodes.definition: Pointing the foot down, as in a calf raise.
nodes.includes: Standing, seated, donkey and single-leg calf raises.

nodes.label: Dorsiflexion
nodes.definition: Lifting the toes towards the shin.
nodes.includes: Tibialis raises, banded dorsiflexion.

nodes.label: Ankle inversion and eversion
nodes.definition: Turning the sole inward or outward.
nodes.includes: Banded inversion and eversion, side-lying foot raises.

nodes.label: Trunk movement
nodes.definition: Movements in which the trunk itself moves.
nodes.includes: Flexion, extension, rotation and side flexion.

nodes.label: Trunk flexion
nodes.definition: Curling the ribcage towards the pelvis.
nodes.includes: Crunches, cable crunches, sit-ups, reverse crunches.
nodes.excludes: Leg raises that mainly flex the hip (Hip flexion).

nodes.label: Trunk extension
nodes.definition: Arching the spine or lifting the trunk against gravity.
nodes.includes: Back extensions, reverse hyperextensions, Superman.

nodes.label: Trunk rotation
nodes.definition: Turning the ribcage relative to the pelvis against resistance.
nodes.includes: Cable woodchops, Russian twists, rotational throws.

nodes.label: Trunk lateral flexion
nodes.definition: Bending the trunk sideways against resistance.
nodes.includes: Side bends, weighted side bends, hanging side tilts.

nodes.label: Trunk stability
nodes.definition: Exercises that resist unwanted trunk movement.
nodes.includes: Anti-extension, anti-rotation, anti-lateral flexion.
nodes.excludes: Movements in which the trunk is the mover.

nodes.label: Anti-extension
nodes.definition: Resisting arching of the lower back.
nodes.includes: Planks, rollouts, dead bugs, body saws.

nodes.label: Anti-rotation
nodes.definition: Resisting twisting of the trunk.
nodes.includes: Pallof presses, bird dogs, single-arm planks.

nodes.label: Anti-lateral flexion
nodes.definition: Resisting sideways bending of the trunk.
nodes.includes: Suitcase carries, side planks, single-arm overhead holds.

nodes.label: Carries
nodes.definition: Moving while holding a load.
nodes.includes: Bilateral and unilateral carries.

nodes.label: Bilateral carry
nodes.definition: Walking with equal loads in both hands, on both shoulders or at the front.
nodes.includes: Farmer's carries, front-rack carries, yoke carries.

nodes.label: Unilateral carry
nodes.definition: Walking with a load on one side or in one arm.
nodes.includes: Suitcase carries, waiter's carries, offset carries.

nodes.label: Conditioning and locomotion
nodes.definition: Repeated movement that raises heart rate and trains work capacity.
nodes.includes: Running, ergometers, skipping, sled work, crawling and whole-body circuits.

nodes.label: Walking and running
nodes.definition: Moving on foot at any pace.
nodes.includes: Treadmill and outdoor walking, running and sprinting; incline walking.

nodes.label: Ergometer work
nodes.definition: Continuous or interval work on a cardio machine.
nodes.includes: Bike, rower, cross-trainer, ski ergometer, stair climber.
nodes.excludes: Running on a treadmill (Walking and running), which is a locomotion pattern.

nodes.label: Skipping
nodes.definition: Repeated small jumps over a rope.
nodes.includes: Single, double and alternate-foot skipping.

nodes.label: Sled push and pull
nodes.definition: Moving a loaded sled by pushing or pulling.
nodes.includes: Sled push, sled drag, backward drag.

nodes.label: Crawling
nodes.definition: Moving on hands and feet or hands and knees.
nodes.includes: Bear, crab and leopard crawls.

nodes.label: Whole-body conditioning
nodes.definition: Multi-joint circuits and drills not covered by another conditioning pattern.
nodes.includes: Burpees, battle ropes, mountain climbers, thrusters.

nodes.label: Power and plyometrics
nodes.definition: Fast, forceful movements and jumps.
nodes.includes: Jumps, upper-body plyometrics and explosive lifts.

nodes.label: Vertical jump
nodes.definition: Jumping upward and landing.
nodes.includes: Box jumps, squat jumps, tuck jumps.

nodes.label: Horizontal jump
nodes.definition: Jumping forward or bounding.
nodes.includes: Broad jumps, bounds, hurdle hops.

nodes.label: Lateral jump
nodes.definition: Jumping or bounding side to side.
nodes.includes: Skater jumps, lateral box jumps.

nodes.label: Upper-body plyometric
nodes.definition: Fast throws, slams and explosive push-ups.
nodes.includes: Medicine ball slams and throws, clap push-ups.

nodes.label: Explosive lift
nodes.definition: Fast lifts that finish with a hip and knee extension.
nodes.includes: Cleans, snatches, high pulls, push presses with leg drive.

nodes.label: Wrist and grip
nodes.definition: Movements and holds at the wrist and hand.
nodes.includes: Wrist flexion and extension, forearm rotation, grip holds.

nodes.label: Wrist flexion
nodes.definition: Curling the hand towards the forearm.
nodes.includes: Wrist curls, plate pinches with wrist movement.

nodes.label: Wrist extension
nodes.definition: Lifting the back of the hand towards the forearm.
nodes.includes: Reverse wrist curls.

nodes.label: Forearm rotation
nodes.definition: Turning the palm up or down.
nodes.includes: Pronation and supination with a dumbbell or bar.
nodes.excludes: Elbow flexion with a supinated grip.

nodes.label: Grip hold
nodes.definition: Holding a position or object with the hand muscles.
nodes.includes: Dead hangs, plate pinches, towel hangs.
nodes.note: Dead hang is classed here and has category core in the seed.

nodes.label: Mobility and stretching
nodes.definition: Work aimed at range of motion rather than load.
nodes.includes: Static stretches, dynamic mobility, spinal mobility, soft tissue release.
nodes.excludes: Strength exercises done through a long range.

nodes.label: Static stretch
nodes.definition: Holding a lengthened position for time.
nodes.includes: Hamstring, hip flexor and chest stretches; child's pose.

nodes.label: Dynamic mobility
nodes.definition: Moving through a joint range under control without load.
nodes.includes: Leg swings, world's greatest stretch, arm circles.

nodes.label: Spinal mobility
nodes.definition: Moving the spine through flexion, extension or rotation.
nodes.includes: Cat-cow, thoracic extension, open-book rotation.
nodes.excludes: Loaded trunk flexion or extension (Trunk movement).

nodes.label: Soft tissue release
nodes.definition: Self-applied pressure with a roller or ball.
nodes.includes: Foam rolling, ball release.
nodes.excludes: Conditional on owner approval (see equipment list).

nodes.label: Neck movement
nodes.definition: Movements of the head and neck.
nodes.includes: Flexion, extension and side flexion.

nodes.label: Neck flexion
nodes.definition: Nodding the head forward against resistance.
nodes.includes: Harness, plate and manual-resistance flexion; chin tucks.

nodes.label: Neck extension
nodes.definition: Tilting the head back against resistance.
nodes.includes: Harness, plate and manual-resistance extension.

nodes.label: Neck lateral flexion
nodes.definition: Tilting the ear towards the shoulder against resistance.
nodes.includes: Manual-resistance and band side flexion.
